source: wsrs-tso docs/vocabulary-design.md, decisions of 20 October 2026 (Elder Bendio). Not yet approved by Stephanie.

categories.label: Addiction
categories.definition: Treatment, recovery support and harm reduction for alcohol, drugs and nicotine.

categories.label: Case Management
categories.definition: A person who works with someone over time to plan and coordinate help across several needs.

categories.label: Clothing/Household
categories.definition: Free or low-cost clothing, furniture, bedding and household goods.

categories.label: Domestic Violence
categories.definition: Safety, shelter, advocacy and support for people harmed by a partner or family member, and for survivors of abuse.

categories.label: Education
categories.definition: Learning: diplomas and GED, English, literacy, college and trade schools, scholarships, life skills, money skills, parenting classes and preschool.

categories.label: Employment
categories.definition: Finding and keeping work: job search, placement, and training tied to a job.

categories.label: Filing Assistance
categories.definition: Help completing applications and claims for public benefits, and free tax preparation.

categories.label: Financial Assistance
categories.definition: Money for a specific need, such as emergencies or medical costs. Rent help is under Housing, and utility bills under Utilities.

categories.label: Food
categories.definition: Food to take home or eat on site, food benefits such as WIC, and pet food.

categories.label: Homeless Services
categories.definition: Shelter and daily needs for people without housing: beds, meals, showers, laundry, mail and storage.

categories.label: Housing
categories.definition: Finding, keeping or paying for a place to live: rentals, rent and deposit help, vouchers, transitional housing, shelters, home buying and repairs.

categories.label: ID Replacement
categories.definition: Getting a birth certificate, ID card, driver license or Social Security card.

categories.label: Legal
categories.definition: Free or low-cost legal help, including immigration, record clearing and identity theft.

categories.label: Long-term care
categories.definition: Help for people who can't fully care for themselves: in-home care, adult day programs, respite for the carer, and finding assisted living or a care home.

categories.label: Medical/Dental/Vision
categories.definition: Health care for body, teeth and eyes, including pregnancy care and early intervention.

categories.label: Mental Health
categories.definition: Counseling, treatment, crisis help and suicide prevention, support groups, and grief and trauma care.

categories.label: Transportation
categories.definition: Getting from place to place: transit, reduced fares, rides, and car repair help.

categories.label: Utilities
categories.definition: Help paying for power, gas, water, phone and internet, and low-cost phone and internet service.

groups.label: Children and youth
groups.counts: It is designed for children or teens, not just open to them

groups.label: Disabled Persons
groups.who: People with a physical, mental, intellectual or developmental disability
groups.counts: Its service is shaped by the disability (equipment, accessible transport, disability rights, specialized programs); being accessible is not enough

groups.label: Families with children
groups.who: Parents or guardians with children living with them
groups.counts: It serves the family together (family shelters, family programs); simply allowing children does not count

groups.label: Homeless people
groups.who: People without a regular place to live, including in shelters, cars or outdoors
groups.counts: It is designed for people without housing

groups.label: Immigrants and refugees
groups.who: People born in another country, including refugees, asylum seekers and those without status
groups.counts: It is designed for them (resettlement, immigration law, English for newcomers)

groups.label: Medically vulnerable
groups.who: People too ill or frail to manage in an ordinary shelter or on the street
groups.counts: It provides care or shelter suited to their health (medical respite, medically vulnerable shelters)

groups.label: Men
groups.counts: It is designed for men, usually men-only shelters and programs

groups.label: Native Americans
groups.who: Members or descendants of tribes and pueblos
groups.counts: It is run by or for Native communities, including tribal programs and Indian Health Service

groups.label: People with a criminal record
groups.who: Anyone with a record, recently released or not
groups.counts: It helps with the record's effects (reentry, record clearing, employers who hire people with records)

groups.label: Pet owners
groups.counts: It provides for the pet (pet food, pet shelter in a crisis, pet-friendly shelters)

groups.label: Pregnant or postpartum
groups.who: Pregnant, or up to a year after birth
groups.counts: It provides pregnancy or newborn care or support

groups.label: Seniors
groups.who: Older adults; each program sets its own age (55, 60, 62), stated in the resource
groups.counts: It is designed for older adults

groups.label: Single parents
groups.counts: It is designed for single parents (scholarships, programs)

groups.label: Spanish speaking
groups.counts: Someone can actually serve the person in Spanish, or services or materials are in Spanish

groups.label: Students
groups.who: People enrolled in school or college
groups.counts: It is for students (campus pantries, student help centers, student veteran hubs)

groups.label: Uninsured
groups.counts: It serves people without insurance (free clinics, sliding-fee care)

groups.label: Veterans
groups.who: People who served in the U.S. military, and sometimes their families
groups.counts: It is designed for veterans or their families (VA services, veteran housing)

groups.label: Women
groups.counts: It is designed for women, usually women-only shelters and programs

groups.label: Young adults
groups.counts: It is designed for young adults (aging out of foster care, Job Corps, youth transitional housing)
